My Mum is in her 81'st year - bear with me - and she has had a go at one or two "experiences" in VR since I got my Vive last year. I thought she would love to try this. Within five minutes she was back at the place she grew up, giggling and squeeling with delight. Then she went up "Tandle Hill" and suddenly I noticed she wasn't laughing anymore.

I asked her if she was ok, and I noticed she was quietly crying and shaking. "What's the MATTER"?, I asked.

"I haven't been here since I was a little girl; this is so wonderful - thank you so much, I never thought I would ever come here ever again".

THAT, my friends, is worth the cost of the Vive itself.


Pro's: Become Superman/Supergirl and go where you like; visit your own house; go to that place you always wanted to; sit on cliffs and scare yourself to death; "Leap" from tall buildings; Take off and go into space then land on the other side of the planet; go to that holiday place again (without the traffic jams); play a game of "can I find it again from space without getting lost on the way down"; save your own favourites and jump straight there next time. Change the time of day or night by dragging the Sun across the sky. All for FREE !!!!

IN MY OPINION - the best and most enduring VR experience ever, and probably for a long time to come.

Cons:

Well, not really any, but I would like to see the following features added as this gem is polished:

To be able to leave human scale on ALL THE TIME. I know it is great to feel like Gulliver, walking between the mountains or skyscrapers, but for immersion I'd like to be able to leave my eyes 70mm apart and view the Earth in normal scale (at least have the option).

Ability to reverse the "BRAKE" option so that you are slow by default and you pull the trigger to accellerate; I, personally, want to take it all in, not rush off.

I am not bothered about the comfort mode and prefer not to use it, but for those that get motion sickness, an option to change the size of the "tunnel" view to suit.

I for one, don't mind that you can't text-search for places to "teleport" to; searching adds to the enjoyment, but I'll expect a lot of people would prefer the option.

I know there's mirror mode, which you can modify to show just left/right eye as a circle on the screen, but for your friends to be able to view the experience full screen. I appreciate this could affect FPS etc, so just the option would be nice. 

Graphics settings, perhaps.

Oh, I don't know, fly to and around the Moon next maybe?  ;-D

These are not complaints, just hopes for the future. This App is nothing short of incredible!

Google earth VR is one of those applications that falls into the category of "things I will return to over and over" - for both useful familiarisation with a location to just aimless virtual meandering.  

I would advise switching human scale on, so that when you "touch down" everything around you is to scale.  The moment you fly up the scale sneakily changes such that a city more resembles a scale model leaving you to stand head high with sky scrapers or fly up more and stride over districts, crouching and peering over buildings and features that capture your interest.

GE comes with comfort mode on by default, which means that the centre is in focus as you move, but the outer areas are blur until you are at a standstill.  Personally I prefer to take that off, but I can see why some find it a bit much as you shoot off into the sky like some middle aged super hero.

There are also some nice touches like being able to drag the sun across the sky to change the lighting, and a handy earth 'lollipop' to help you easily get roughly to where you want to go.

Google earth VR is a happy marriage of a lot of historic work and technology that has been around for its own purposes,  and some added talent and serendipity to bring all of that to VR.  If you are (like my wife was) expecting photo realisim as you stand on some Tokyo street, then bear in mind the 3D assets are the same as you see in any other Google Earth incarnation -  as amazing as they are, they are the result of very ambitious arial scanning and as such at human scale the models have that melted cheese appearance.  It would be nice to see street view intergration as an optional layer, one where you stepped into and were contstrained to the Rails of the aquisition vehicle, until you opted back out to full 3D freedom.

Another ommision is a way to search for places or landmarks.. Its a pain to have to leave VR to get your bearings and re-enter and find manually.

I don't know how far the team intends on taking this project, but I hope they continue to push the great work forward, add a fun interface for viewing local photography or other layers; and maybe one day get to more frivolous features like believable ambient noises based on the locality, businesses , population and features such as forests, oceans and parks nearby -  I have to say, as silly as I look, I have even used GE VR to jog around Central Park... Google earth is what pretty is all about. If you like staring at cut flowers in a vase, then you'll love google earth. If you want to take advantage of the mind-blowingly awesome capabilities of earth in VR... Forget it. Google clearly fell in love with the clunky spatial controllers of the Vive and created a dogs-breakfast of a user interface.

Clearly google has lost the plot when it comes to usability, so the wonderful aspects of being able to see the earth up close are lost to the unusable controls, which are frustrating and imprecise when it comes to navigating.

I get it - really I do. You want a room level experience and you created it. That's nice. So what if I want to sit and just view things from a usable angle? Oh... That's a pain. Adjust steam floor levels within the app? Too hard. Switch on a keyboard and just use mechanical instructions to tell you what I want to do? Verbotten.

Google Earth is typical of most VR junk out at the moment. The programmers are so stuck in their mindset that they have to do everything VR that they lose track of why we use computers in the first place. Maybe I don't want to point and shoot. I just want spin and move with thumb controllers or the likes. I don't want to swing my arms around all the time like I have control issues. I just want to absorb the view while controlling things like I can on the desktop.

This app misses the plot. I'd give it one star for user interface, but the pretty graphics, if you're willing to wait minutes for them to load, are still pretty... I'll give it two starts and a "Not Recommended" until they figure out what a user interface is.
